action.rationale: Fresh start with dim=10 and a large budget of 2000 on a cheap, deterministic problem; with budget ≥ 20·dim (=200) we should probe first to read the landscape. Allocating ~12% (~240) to probes seeds the archive and guides method choice before committing.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin: P5 cosine = 1.0 (reliable gradients), P4 rel_gain = 0.978 and endpoint_y_spread = 0.124 (< 0.3), with P3 quadratic R² ≈ 0.96. Polishing the incumbent y=2078.59 with L-BFGS-B should converge quickly on this deterministic 10-D problem.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin (P5 cosine_min = 1.0; P4 endpoint_y_spread = 0.124), so a local solver is best. L-BFGS-B just achieved a new best 154.07 at eval 637, has improved by 1924.52 over 400 evals, and is not exhausted, so continuing should yield further reductions efficiently. With 1,362 evals left, another round of L-BFGS-B is the quickest path toward convergence.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin (P5 cosine_min = 1.0; P4 gain = 0.9785 with y_spread = 0.124), so lbfgsb remains appropriate. The active lbfgsb is not exhausted and still improved last round (154.07 → 151.775) with stall_evals only 4 (< 2×round_size).

Probes show a smooth single basin (P5 cosine=1.0; P4 gain=0.9785, y_spread=0.124), favoring lbfgsb. The active lbfgsb isn’t exhausted and improved 1.44 last round (151.775→150.336), so another round should reduce the value further.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin (P5 cosine = 1.0; P4 endpoint_y_spread = 0.124), so lbfgsb is appropriate. The active lbfgsb is still improving (stall_evals = 6 < 2×round_size) and not exhausted, with best down to 149.269 from 150.133 last round. Continuing should yield further steady gains without restart overhead.

Probes indicate a smooth single basin (P5 cosine = 1.0; P4 y_spread = 0.124, rel_gain = 0.979), and LBFGSB is still improving (149.269 → 149.152 last round) with no stall (stall_evals = 7 < 200). Continuing should squeeze more improvement efficiently before considering any switch.

lbfgsb has exhausted at y=149.15 (state.exhausted=true after 869 evals), so this basin is finished. With 893 evals left on a smooth problem (P5 cosine=1.0; P4 endpoint_y_spread=0.124), we’ll do one IPOP-style CMA-ES restart from a diverse point to check for a better basin, then polish if it wins.

Probes show a smooth single basin (P5 cosine=1.0; P4 gain=0.9785, y_spread=0.124), and lbfgsb already reached 149.15 at eval 1098. CMA-ES used 100 evals with 0 improvement (stall_evals=121), so further exploration is unlikely to help; stopping saves budget without sacrificing quality.
